explicit_user_instruction.instruction: Eliminate all causes and fix the automation stopping problem.
explicit_user_instruction.effect: The optimizer must remove every observed removable stop cause across the full existing 19-role pool, not continue one-role canaries or point-in-time re-enable cycles.

finding.dominant_operational_cause: Repeated roles that stopped did so around the 62-63 second boundary and frequently left no current durable receipt; surviving bounded roles returned in the 20-41 second band.
contributing_causes: stale bootstrap wording that ordered run-to-hard-runtime behavior
unbounded same-run retry/backoff, waiting and optional second work units
repository-only lifecycle changes without uniform physical prompt alignment
optimizer scheduled before late roles, allowing late post-run disables to miss the next slot
condition_watch used as a persistence proxy despite not proving hourly useful execution
point-in-time 19/19 repair being recorded without two-boundary survival

evidence.survivor_example: open_source revision48 completed artifact/checkpoint/LATEST/receipt in about 41 seconds with termination=bounded_slice_complete_recurring_open

finding.causal_precision: The internal platform actor remains unknown, but the approximately one-minute trigger state and removable contributing paths are sufficiently evidenced to require prevention rather than more blind re-enable-only cycles.

prior_revision_13.method: checkpoint-first single-effect-chain applied to six observed stopped roles
prior_revision_13.why_superseded_as_global_plan: It is a useful local mechanism but does not remove lifecycle contradictions and time-boundary risk across all 19 roles, does not move the optimizer after late roles, and still permits untreated roles to enter the same failure state. The user's new instruction requires all causes to be eliminated across the full pool.

Apply the RUN_LIFECYCLE schedule map, including optimizer minute59; exact-readback every changed task.
Confirm 19/19 enabled, prompt-aligned and schedule-aligned; confirm no replacement tasks, pool reduction or protected monitor change.
Persist a compact application receipt and start two-boundary survival verification.
Only after the physical apply, perform a bounded semantic role/method optimization that fits the optimizer lifecycle budget.
prompt_template_requirements: Read current repository semantic control first, then automation_control/RUN_LIFECYCLE.json.
Semantic control defines WHAT; RUN_LIFECYCLE defines one-invocation budget and normal-return behavior.
Execute exactly one bounded Phase-1 slice, persist/read back exact continuation, leave enabled_desired=true, never mutate scheduler, and return before 45 seconds.
Never continue until a hard runtime/tool stop, wait/poll/backoff in the same run, or claim completion from a slice/blocker/no-change result.

verification.on_failure: Immediately re-enable the same task, inspect its duration/last write/final marker/error path, tighten only that role's micro-slice or compact-write plan, and preserve the full pool. Do not revert to hard-boundary behavior, condition-watch as a blanket fix, or pool reduction.
verification.phase1_closure: Scheduler persistence is necessary but not sufficient; all semantic zero-Work, zero-finite-quota, zero-cost, usefulness, conflict and authority gates remain fail-closed.

rollback.allowed: Only restore an individual schedule or neutral bootstrap wording if matched evidence proves the new value harms useful output, while keeping the task enabled and lifecycle bounded.
rollback.forbidden: Never restore run-until-hard-stop wording, blind repeated retries, early optimizer placement, blanket condition-watch, role disablement, pool reduction, primary/protected mutation, finite quota or cost.

exact_next_action: Apply RUN_LIFECYCLE revision1 and PROMPT_LIFECYCLE_ALIGNMENT revision2 physically across all 19 existing managed tasks: fresh inventory, re-enable, prompt alignment, end-of-hour schedule map with optimizer minute59, exact readback, then two-boundary verification. The corrected 19-role mapping is mandatory.
